title: Importing Spells
description: Learn how to borrow code libraries written by other wizards using the import statement!

content.value: You don't need to write every single code function yourself. Python has a huge library of pre-written code (called Modules) that other programmers wrote! You can borrow their work using the `import` statement.
If you want to roll a dice, pick a random card, or select a random option in a game, you can import the `random` module!

import random

# Roll a 6-sided dice:
dice_roll = random.randint(1, 6)
print("You rolled a:", dice_roll)
The `math` module gives you access to advanced math operations like calculating square roots (`math.sqrt`) or getting the exact value of Pi!

import math
print(math.pi)          # Prints 3.141592653589793
print(math.sqrt(25))    # Prints 5.0
The `time` module can make the computer pause and wait before running the next lines of code using `time.sleep()`.

import time
print("Starting timer...")
time.sleep(1)
print("1 second passed!")

quiz.question: Which keyword is used to load a pre-written library module in Python?
quiz.explain: `import` loads a ready-made module so you can use its tools without writing them yourself.

quiz.question: Which module would you import to generate a random number?
quiz.explain: The `random` module makes random numbers. `math` is for calculations and `time` is for clocks and delays.
